title: Pricing memo: ad-tier vs premium for IPL
persona: Rajesh, growth manager on Disney+ Hotstar IPL
scenario: IPL streams free with ads in India this season. Premium-tier upgrades are down 22% from last year. Growth wants to test a ‘mid-tier’ at ₹149/month: cleaner ads, 1080p, 1 device. Your VP needs a memo by Friday that frames the experiment, the success criteria, the cannibalisation risk on premium, and the smallest possible test that gives a clean read in 3 weeks.
badPrompt: write a memo about a new mid-tier pricing experiment for hotstar
badOutput:
Memo: Mid-tier Pricing

Introduce a new ₹149 tier with cleaner ads. Test against existing tiers. Measure conversion and revenue. Look for opportunities to grow ARPU.

hints.title: Force a falsifiable hypothesis
hints.body: ‘State the hypothesis as: if X, then Y, measured by Z.’ Without this, memos are wish-lists.

hints.title: Make cannibalisation explicit
hints.body: Demand a specific cannibalisation risk on premium with a kill-switch metric. Pricing tests fail when this is buried.

checks.tip: Frame the artifact, a memo, not a pitch.
Anchor the topic, pricing tier experiment.
Anchor the context, IPL free-with-ads, premium down 22%.
Use the specific tier shape, ₹149, 1080p, cleaner ads, 1 device.
Lock the test duration, 3 weeks for a clean read.
Force a cannibalisation risk with a kill-switch metric.
Reference the VP audience and Friday deadline.
Force a falsifiable hypothesis, ‘if X, then Y, measured by Z’.
Specify the memo sections, hypothesis, metrics, risks, success criteria.
Lock a length budget, 1-pager, otherwise the memo sprawls.

tipIfLow: Pricing memos die when they're vibes-based. The unlock is a falsifiable hypothesis (if/then/measured-by), a named cannibalisation risk with a kill-switch, and a defined test window. ‘Test a new tier’ is not a memo. ‘If ₹149 cleaner-ads tier converts >X% of free users without dropping premium >Y%, ship it’ is.
goldPrompt: Act as a pricing-experiment designer. I'm Rajesh, growth on Disney+ Hotstar IPL. Premium upgrades down 22% YoY because IPL streams free-with-ads. Growth wants a ₹149 mid-tier (cleaner ads, 1080p, 1 device). VP needs a memo by Friday. Open with the hypothesis as 'If [treatment] then [outcome] measured by [metric] over [window]'. Then: 3-week test design with a named cannibalisation risk on premium AND a kill-switch metric (e.g., '>5% premium downgrades pauses the test'). End with success criteria thresholds. Refuse hand-wavy 'we'll see how it goes'.
